articles.title_orig: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings to turn workplace discussions into plans and tasks
articles.title_zh: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings to turn workplace discussions into plans and tasks
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic announced new workplace features on Tuesday, including Claude Meetings, which brings Claude into video calls to begin working on tasks while participants are still talking. The company also unveiled Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets.
The launch of Anthropic’s new productivity-focused features comes just a few weeks after OpenAI unveiled a series of workplace tools that allow users to collaborate with ChatGPT to do things like visualize company information and create presentations, as both companies compete to turn their products into office suites of sorts to take on Microsoft and Google. Meta is also joining the competition with its Muse AI agent, which can build mini-apps on the fly to help users complete specific tasks.
With Claude Meetings, teams can add Claude to a video call as a visible participant. Claude then follows the conversation and gets to work on tasks in real time. As participants talk, it can draft the plan being discussed, map out a timeline on a whiteboard, answer questions in the meeting chat, and access connected work apps to retrieve information, such as last year’s figures. After the call, the meeting notes, action items, and other materials Claude created are available in claude.ai.
The work that comes out of a meeting usually starts after everyone hangs up, but with this new feature, teams can turn discussions into actions in real time, Anthropic says.
Claude identifies itself as a meeting participant and posts a notice in the meeting chat. It won’t join calls with external guests unless authorized by an admin, and will automatically leave if an external guest joins.
Claude Meetings is launching in beta on Team and Enterprise plans. At launch, it works with Google Meet, with support for additional plans expected to follow.
As for Claude Whiteboards, Anthropic describes the feature as a collaborative board where teams can talk through a plan and have Claude turn it into an organized visual workspace with timelines and deadlines.
The company notes that many people already brainstorm with Claude, but that in order to share their results with others, they would have to copy-paste them somewhere else. Now, a team can work directly with Claude on the same board in real time.
When the brainstorm is done, Claude can turn the board into a doc or a slide deck. Additionally, Whiteboards also work inside Claude Meetings, so the board builds while people talk, Anthropic says.
Claude Whiteboards is available in beta on paid plans, on web, desktop, and mobile.
The company also launched Claude Sheets, which lets teams create and collaboratively edit spreadsheets with Claude. A team can ask it to build a campaign tracker or hiring budget, and Claude will then generate a working spreadsheet.
Anthropic says Claude handles the initial setup of trackers and budgets, while allowing teams to continue refining and updating the same spreadsheet. Each spreadsheet can include multiple tabs, formulas, formatting, and dropdown menus. Claude also makes edits directly in cells alongside the team, and outlines each change so users can see what it did.
Claude Sheets is available in beta on paid plans, on web, desktop and mobile.
Anthropic also announced that Claude Data, formerly known as Claude Dashboards, is now generally available. The feature connects Claude to systems that companies use to keep their numbers, like a data warehouse or CRM. Users can ask questions, and Claude responds with dashboards, written data stories, or narrated videos.
Additionally, the company announced interactive connectors that open the full version of apps like Adobe, Atlassian, and HubSpot inside Claude. Anthropic notes that teams can now open these apps directly alongside their Claude conversations and ask the assistant to work within them, essentially bringing existing workflows into the same workspace.

articles.title_orig: Google Fi brings back network switching with ‘secondary’ partner, expands W+ beyond Pixel
articles.title_zh: Google Fi brings back network switching with ‘secondary’ partner, expands W+ beyond Pixel
articles.content_orig:
Google Fi Wireless is rolling out a big update today with the return of network switching thanks to a “secondary” partner.
At the beginning, Project Fi was known for giving subscribers access to both T-Mobile and Sprint networks. Over time, the second partner went away, leaving one predominant network.
Google Fi is now bringing back a second partner as part of its new “super network.” Most users will be on the “Primary network,” but Google Fi will automatically switch users to the “Secondary network” if it meaningfully improves performance with so-called “smart thresholds” for doing so. At launch, there is no manual switching.
Google is not naming the second network today, but did share that Ultra Wideband is supported. Officially, you are switching between “two of America’s fastest 5G networks.”
Fi Wireless does note that users have top priority, so data is never deprioritized on the Primary network. Meanwhile, there’s “highest QCI priority” on the backup network that means subscribers are among the last to be slowed down when there’s congestion. This is also available internationally when local partner networks are available with the Flexible and Unlimited Premium plans.
Network switching will first be supported on Pixel 9 and newer devices that have a Google Fi eSIM (and no other SIM active). It makes use of Android’s Multiple Enabled Profiles (MEP) eSIM technology that allows for two carrier profiles on a single chip.
The Google Fi app gains a “Your super network” card in the Home tab that shows whether you’re connected to the Primary or Secondary network. “See activity” lets you view switching history and when it last occurred. Google will also note if you’re in range of W+ networks.
Google today is also expanding its Wi-Fi Auto Connect+ network beyond Pixel phones to select Samsung Galaxy (S23, Fold/Flip 5, and newer) and modern Motorola phones. These premium Wi-Fi networks are available in millions of airports, malls, stores, and restaurants. The connection happens automatically, with the Google Fi Virtual Carrier Network encrypting data.
The final update today sees the companion app gain “Ask Fi.” This AI-powered chat is meant to quickly provide answers and guided troubleshooting for common issues. You can request human support with seamless handoff that keeps the chat context.
These Google Fi updates start rolling out today, with network switching seeing gradual availability. This launch is accompanied by several deals:

Micron's ( MU ) valuation has reached a level where it's simply too cheap to ignore given its fundamentals, says Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider.
Schneider reiterated his $1,250 price target on the once red-hot AI momentum trade. It assumes about 70% upside from current levels.
"We also believe risk/reward is becoming more attractive for Neutral-rated Micron in light of the high probability of strong free cash flow in the coming quarters," Schneider said.
Micron is currently approaching tangible book value, Schneider noted. When a stock trades below tangible book value, investors value the company at less than the estimated value of its assets after subtracting its liabilities and intangible assets.
In a sense, the market is saying the company's physical and financial assets are worth more than the entire company's stock market value.
That seems to be bordering on an unwarranted disconnect , at least in assessing Schneider's work on the chip player.
Micron's stock is down 17% over the past month amid fears that a blue wave on Election Day could slow the build-out of AI infrastructure. That could have ramifications for orders for Micron's memory chips.
The rout has brought Micron's forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio down to an almost laughable 4.2 times, according to Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data. Keep in mind Micron is coming off a quarter of strong demand amid memory chip shortages driving up prices.
The Street still expects Micron to grow earnings by at least 17% in its next fiscal year.

articles.title_orig: Steam Deck performance gets a reality check with Valve's new FPS data
articles.title_zh: Steam Deck performance gets a reality check with Valve's new FPS data
articles.content_orig:
Since Valve announced its Steam Deck Verified program in 2021 , players have found that a game’s “Verified” status doesn’t always match how well it actually runs on the handheld. Now, new Steam Deck frame rate data being shared by Valve itself can help players dig deeper into the performance they can expect from many Steam Deck games.
Valve has been collecting anonymized frame rate data from Steam players who opt in since February . Yesterday evening, the company announced it has started sharing that data on many Steam Store pages as averages and histograms for both the Steam Deck and Steam Deck OLED.
Valve acknowledges that players enabling VSync or frame rate limits can bias the collected data somewhat and that the measurements don’t account for custom in-game settings that Steam Deck users may tinker with to get a game running. Regardless, Valve says it has nonetheless “found that the framerate data consolidates around relatively narrow ranges.”
This kind of data can be extremely useful for distinguishing between the wide range of performance levels that can exist among “Verified” Steam Deck games. Both Cyberpunk 2077 and Skyrim: Special Edition earn the same Steam Deck Verified badge, for instance, but the former sees average Deck frame rates in the 30–40 FPS range, while the latter usually achieves 50–60 FPS on the hardware.
Valve’s frame rate data is even more useful for games that the company insists are “Unsupported” on Steam Deck because their “graphics setting cannot be configured to run well” on the hardware or because Valve is “still working on adding support for this game.” Despite warnings like these, games like Starfield , Silent Hill 2 , and Assassin’s Creed Syndicate, to name just a few, all show extremely playable frame rates reported by actual Steam Deck users. Assassin’s Creed Syndicate in particular approaches a 60 FPS average on the Steam Deck OLED hardware despite its “Unsupported” status.
Frame rate data can also be useful for judging the single-player modes of games whose multiplayer doesn’t work under SteamOS. Watch Dogs 2 , for example, is officially Unsupported on Steam Deck because of anti-cheat compatibility issues, but Steam Deck players report averages of 40+ FPS on the game’s single-player modes.
Of course, collecting and averaging frame rate data for the Steam Deck(s) is made simpler by their set hardware configuration. When it comes to communicating expected frame rates for the wide range of hardware in more generalized gaming PCs, Valve says it is “always looking for new ways to help developers understand the experiences customers are having with their games.”
Back in April, JSON files buried in the Steam client pointed to a potential Steam “Framerate Estimator” tool that could let users “Select an App and a PC config to get a chart of estimated framerates, based on the framerates of other Steam users,” according to strings contained within. That could be incredibly useful for Steam users who want to go beyond the listed Minimum and Recommended hardware requirements without relying on shady-looking third-party FPS-estimator websites . In the meantime, is sharing average frame rate data for the fixed-configuration Steam Machine too much to ask?

articles.title_orig: Credit card debt climbs to a record $1.29 trillion, New York Fed research finds
articles.title_zh: Credit card debt climbs to a record $1.29 trillion, New York Fed research finds
articles.content_orig:
Americans are increasingly turning to credit cards as financial pressures mount, new reports show.
Collectively, credit card balances climbed by $22 billion in the third quarter to a record $1.29 trillion, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's latest household debt report , released Tuesday. Balances are up 4.2% from a year earlier.
Total household debt, including mortgages , auto loans and student loans , also expanded by $334 billion for the July-to-September period to a record $19.1 trillion.
"Overall debt has been growing," the New York Fed researchers said on a press call Tuesday. "This does reflect financial hardship out there."
The average credit card balance per consumer now stands at $6,678, up 2.4% year over year, a separate quarterly credit industry insights report from TransUnion found. The number of people with credit cards rose 2% to 178 million from 174.8 million.
Consumers often turn to credit cards in part because they are more accessible than other types of loans — even though the average interest rate on a new credit card offer is about 24%, according to data from LendingTree . Credit card APRs vary depending on the type of card, the issuer and the borrower's creditworthiness.
"Credit cards continue to be one of the most expensive ways to borrow," said Charlie Wise, TransUnion's senior vice president of global research and consulting.
Over time, an increasing share of new credit cards has gone to borrowers with lower incomes and credit scores, and "those accounts are now showing higher levels of distress," the New York Fed researchers said in a corresponding blog post .
Credit card issuers loosened their lending standards during the Covid pandemic, and delinquency rates rose in the years that followed, the New York Fed researchers said on the press call.
"Macroeconomic headwinds — namely high inflation and rising borrowing costs — have squeezed consumers, with inflation outpacing wage growth for low-income brackets," according to the New York Fed.
Meanwhile, the cost of living continues to climb, with Americans paying more for essentials such as groceries and gas.
Stubborn inflation has now stretched on for years, putting many households in an affordability squeeze. Costs for goods and services rose more than expected again in October, the Bureau of Labor Statistics also reported Tuesday.
"Higher prices and higher rates have pushed more people into debt," said Ted Rossman, principal consumer finance analyst at Money Management International, a nonprofit credit counseling agency.
Balances have continued to swell in the wake of the pandemic, and even though the growth rate is now slowing, "from a household finance standpoint, a lot of damage has been done," Rossman said.
The reports come on the heels of the Democrats' strong midterm results, when many voters expressed their dissatisfaction with the U.S. economy , according to Kyle Moore, chief economist at the nonpartisan think tank The Century Foundation.
"The throughline connecting so many of Tuesday's outcomes was a recognition that the American economy is failing American families," Moore said, referring to Election Day.

articles.title_orig: Why Did Moscow Police Just Arrest Scores of Teenagers?
articles.title_zh: Why Did Moscow Police Just Arrest Scores of Teenagers?
articles.content_orig:
Moscow police arrested scores of “nonconformist” teenagers on Saturday night in a massive raid on the popular nightlife district of Kitai-Gorod.
Telegram news outlets put the number of detainees at between 100 and 300 , with most estimates ranging from 150 to 200.
Eyewitnesses said as many as 15 police vans arrived in Kitai-Gorod at around 8:00 p.m. local time, shortly after which officers started “indiscriminately” arresting people.
One detainee told the RBC news website that police stopped their group of friends on the way to a clothing store, asked their ages and ordered them to get into one of the vans.
“We weren’t drinking, smoking, or anything,” the detainee said. “We sat in the van for about an hour and a half. They took us to the Tagansky police station.”
The detainee said police then handed them military draft notices.
A crowd of parents gathered outside the police station. Chants of “freeloaders” and “we’re keeping you here” could be heard in video footage posted online.
The Interior Ministry described the raid as a “preventive” measure to “maintain public order.”
The Ostorozhno Novosti news outlet reported that the police prevented the parents from entering the station, where police were holding at least one child as young as 12.
One detainee told the outlet that police denied the detainees water, and that he witnessed the police officers beat another detainee for smoking an electronic cigarette.
The Telegram news channel Baza, which is believed to have links to the Russian security services, reported that at least 17 people were issued military summonses, while one detainee told Ostorozhno Novosti that everyone around him at the station received one.
“No exceptions. I have a deferment, but I still received a draft notice,” he said.
Idite Lesom (Get Lost), a group that helps Russian men avoid military service, said Sunday that it had received requests for help from two people detained in the raid, both of whom were ordered to appear at the enlistment office on Ulitsa Yablochkova on Monday morning.
At least one person has been sentenced to administrative detention. Magomed Gasanov, 21, spent two nights in police custody after allegedly refusing to show his passport and was sentenced Monday to 13 days in detention for disobeying police, Ostorozhno Novosti reported.
The outlet said Moscow’s Basmanny and Tagansky district courts received 12 cases on Monday involving petty hooliganism and disobeying police, but it could not confirm whether all of them were related to the Kitai-Gorod raids.
Kitai-Gorod, a neighborhood just east of the Kremlin, has become a popular hangout for teenagers from various youth subcultures, especially “nonconformists,” or “ nefors ” for short. “ Nefors ,” a Russian slang term, is used to describe young people who dress unconventionally.
Saturday’s raid was not the first time they’ve faced police action.
Police in July detained dozens of teenagers in the neighborhood. One detainee told Ostorozhno Novosti that officers had asked them what they were doing in Kitai-Gorod, and whether or not they had consumed alcohol or drugs.
“They humiliated us, yelling that we were scumbags. They suggested shaving my head. Then one of the police officers took out a stun gun and started shocking everyone. He shocked my buddy three times with the stun gun,” the detainee told the outlet.
Teenagers interviewed by Bereg, an independent journalism collective, said police have regularly patrolled the area and harassed “ nefors ” since a March 20 attack on students leaving the Moscow Choral Synagogue.
It remains unclear whether any of the teenagers who regularly gather in the area were involved in that attack.
“People have become afraid to come to Kitai-Gorod because there’s one kind of crowd here before 9:00 [in the evening], and a completely different one after that,” one local business owner told Bereg, describing how teenagers in the area frequently drank, used drugs and caused disturbances.
Teenagers interviewed by the outlet said city officials have gradually been closing off their usual gathering spots in the area, leaving them with fewer and fewer places to go.
Yekaterina Mizulina, head of the pro-Kremlin Safe Internet League, questioned why parents had been barred from seeing their children at the police station.
“Even if the teenagers have done something wrong, the police have no right to detain them for more than three hours — especially if they’re sober and their parents (that is, their legal guardians) have come to the station to pick them up,” she wrote.
Lawmaker Nina Ostanina, who chairs the State Duma’s family affairs committee, asked the Interior Ministry for information about the raid, the Vedomosti business daily reported Tuesday, citing her letter.
According to the letter, Ostanina alleged that the police may have violated the rights of some minor detainees by arbitrarily detaining them, holding them for more than three hours and failing to notify their guardians promptly or let them into the police stations where their children were being held.
Eva Merkacheva, a member of Russia’s presidential human rights council, told Vedomosti that young people should be given the right environment in which to spend their time.
“[We need to] actively involve them in some kind of cultural, interesting life that would appeal to them, taking their current interests into account,” she said.
Shura Bogacheva, a journalist who studies youth subcultures, told the newspaper she believed only a small minority of the teenagers who gather in Kitai-Gorod drink or use drugs there.
She called on authorities to give teenagers more places to gather, as they are “increasingly being pushed out of parks and courtyards.”

We are facing unprecedented challenges. Russia's Prosecutor General's Office has designated The Moscow Times as an "undesirable" organization, criminalizing our work and putting our staff at risk of prosecution. This follows our earlier unjust labeling as a "foreign agent."
These actions are direct attempts to silence independent journalism in Russia. The authorities claim our work "discredits the decisions of the Russian leadership." We see things differently: we strive to provide accurate, unbiased reporting on Russia.
We, the journalists of The Moscow Times, refuse to be silenced. But to continue our work, we need your help .
Your support, no matter how small, makes a world of difference. If you can, please support us monthly starting from just $ 2. It's quick to set up, and every contribution makes a significant impact.

articles.title_orig: PlayStation announces end of PC streaming in December
articles.title_zh: PlayStation announces end of PC streaming in December
articles.content_orig:
PlayStation is ending support for the PS Plus app for PC on December 10. This will block users from streaming their PlayStation games to their PC.
PlayStation quietly announced the move in a blog post going over the latest PS Plus offerings. Towards the end, PlayStation says that the PC app is being discontinued due to a lack of interest amongst players, claiming that less than 0.4% of PS Plus Premium members were using it.
“We wanted to let you know that from December 10, we will be retiring the PlayStation Plus app on PC,” the announcement opens.
“PlayStation believes in providing high-quality experiences to our players, and we regularly review offerings to ensure we are focusing on experiences our members value most. With a very small number of eligible PlayStation Plus Premium members (less than 0.4%) using the PlayStation Plus app on PC, making this change allows us to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that more of our members want to use. As a result, the PlayStation Plus cloud streaming app on PC will no longer be available.
“This change does not affect PlayStation Plus memberships or benefits available on PS5 and PS4 consoles. We appreciate everyone who used the app on PC and will be notifying affected users directly.”
This signals an end to being able to play PlayStation console-exclusive titles on PC through the streaming workaround. This feature will now be exclusive to Xbox , which does allow its users to play its games on different platforms (either through streaming, or natively through Play Anywhere).
It also comes as PlayStation has reversed its PC strategy, no longer porting many of its exclusives to PC after their PS5 launch.
This is just one way in which PlayStation is honing in on the most popular ways to play its games. Controversially, it is also ditching physical game releases by 2028 , going digital-only for any games released on its platforms.

articles.title_orig: Pixel Tag tidbits: Surprise NFC, Find Hub setup, & Bellroy keychain cases
articles.title_zh: Pixel Tag tidbits: Surprise NFC, Find Hub setup, & Bellroy keychain cases
articles.content_orig:
The Made by Google 2026 lineup is finally complete with tomorrow’s retail launch of the Pixel Tag . You can find our review here , while there are some additional details about the device since the August announcement.
The Pixel Tag is the first Find Hub tracker with NFC. Google did not mention this connectivity specification in August, with Near Field Communication letting you tap the tracker to the back of your phone to immediately open device settings. The NFC area on the Pixel Tag is below the circular battery door, which you hold down and twist counterclockwise to open.
On Android 17 QPR2, tapping immediately opens the details page. On QPR1, you first get a system notification that you need to click. NFC joins Bluetooth 6.0 with Channel Sounding and Ultra Wideband (UWB).
The setup process adds a new screen after the initial pairing and terms of use. It lets you configure: Notify when left behind, Ring this phone, Edit name, Edit category, and Adjust volume for this tag.
The Pixel Tag has a physical button on the rear side below the battery cover. Clicking twice plays a loud sound on your phone if both devices are nearby. Once found, you can tap the button once to silence, or turn it off from your phone. This feature can be disabled from the Pixel Tag’s device details page on a tracker-by-tracker basis.
Google does not have a first-party case for the Pixel Tag. Instead, it’s working with Made for Google partner Bellroy.
There are two models available from the Google Store, with the first made of silicone. The Bellroy Lite Case Duo costs $24.99 and comes in a pack of two: Mist and Shadow colorways. It wraps everything but the face of the Pixel Tag (and its speaker cutout), while giving you a hole in the corner and color-matching cord.
There’s also the Bellroy Leather Tag Case in Artichoke, Azalea, Black, Pewter, and Red Ochre for $29.99.

articles.title_orig: Israel's new parliament sworn in as leaders compete to form government
articles.title_zh: Israel's new parliament sworn in as leaders compete to form government
articles.content_orig:
Gadi Eisenkot has vowed to oust Benjamin Netanyahu, but still has to get enough parties on board
Israel's new parliament has been sworn in, as opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot seeks to oust caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
The former army chief has been tasked with forming a government after receiving more recommendations from members of the Knesset than Netanyahu, although not all those backing him are willing to govern together.
Eisenkot's bloc of four parties won 48 seats in October's election, while Netanyahu's bloc won 53, leaving both short of a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. He has 28 days to build a coalition, with a possible two-week extension.
Almost half of the new MKs did not serve in the previous parliament, while Arab-led parties have a record number of seats.
Shortly after they were sworn in, Netanyahu and Eisenkot warned parliament about the perils of supporting a government led by the other.
"[And] to those who are thinking of establishing a government that includes supporters of terror and haters of Israel, or that will be dependent on them, I ask you, are you prepared to be dependent on those whose goal is the destruction of the Jewish state?" said Netanyahu, alluding to the prospect of an Eisenkot-led government reliant on support from Arab parties.
He also appealed for the formation of a government of national unity as the only way to confront what he said was the threat of "a nuclear Iran".
Eisenkot sharply criticised Netanyahu's comments.
"I sat and listened to the outgoing prime minister's delusional, divisive, hate-filled and shameful speech, exploiting a state occasion," he said. "I am now even more convinced that he is unfit to remain in office for even one more minute."
The outcome of the election, which was widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu, means there is a period of uncertainty over who will form the next government. Netanyahu will remain caretaker prime minister until then - a process which could take from days to months.
One of the most dramatic results was the performance of Israel's two Arab-led alliances - the United Arab List and the Joint List - which won an unprecedented 19 seats between them following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.
The Arab parties could therefore hold the balance of power, although Netanyahu has ruled out governing with them and three of the parties in Eisenkot's bloc have opposed including them in a coalition.
On Sunday, President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with trying to form a government.
Speaking at the president's residence, the centrist Yashar party leader called for the formation of a "national emergency government" - an implicit appeal to parties to put ideological differences aside to remove Netanyahu from office.
This, he said, would "require creative and unconventional political steps".
Eisenkot said any party or MK prepared to accept four principles could join his proposed government. Those are recognition of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state; accepting the values of the Declaration of Independence; backing mandatory military, national or civilian service for all, including communities currently exempt; and recognising Hamas as a terrorist organisation and committing to dismantling its military and governing capabilities.
The four requirements, however, could present significant obstacles to Eisenkot's potential partners.
The conscription of ultra-Orthodox Jewish men, who are exempt from military service if they are in full-time religious study, was a major election issue.
The ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism (UTJ) and Shas parties, which won 13 seats in total, have fiercely objected to attempts to change the status quo - something that all parties in Eisenkot's bloc campaigned to do.
Eisenkot's four principles are also contentious for the Arab parties. Both emphasise equal national and civic rights for Israel's Arab citizens, who form about 20% of the population; the vast majority of Israeli Arabs are not required to serve in the military; and neither has publicly recognised Hamas as a terrorist organisation.
The Arab parties could, though, help Eisenkot form a minority government. The United Arab List, which won eight seats, has said it is willing to be part of an Eisenkot-led coalition, while the Joint List, which won 11 seats, has offered parliamentary support from the outside.
If Eisenkot accepted such an arrangement, he would still have to persuade other parties in his bloc to agree. Avigdor Lieberman, whose Yisrael Beiteinu party won seven seats, has so far refused to join a minority government dependent on Arab MKs.
In return for their support, the ultra-Orthodox parties would be likely to demand major concessions on military conscription, which might be unacceptable to most of the parties in Eisenkot's bloc.

articles.title_orig: Google Pixel Tag Initial Review: The gold standard for Find Hub trackers, whatever that’s worth
articles.title_zh: Google Pixel Tag Initial Review: The gold standard for Find Hub trackers, whatever that’s worth
articles.content_orig:
Google’s Find Hub had a tumultuous launch for its performance , but also for a lack of clear direction in hardware. Over two years later, that’s finally arriving in the Google Pixel Tag which, even just a few days in, is the obvious gold standard in the race to build an AirTag for Android devices.
There are plenty of really good Android Find Hub trackers on the market. Pebblebee and Chipolo have been long-standing examples of how to build good dual-network trackers that work on both Android and iOS, while Motorola’s Moto Tag series has delivered two Android-only trackers that deliver better performance and more focused features. But even with the Moto Tag, there’s a clear compromise. Features like the ability to ring your phone are tied to a separate app and, in turn, have some inherent clunkiness.
Pixel Tag is the device that finally brings it all together, and it’s brilliant so far.
I’ve only had the Pixel Tag for a week and, frankly, it’s impossible to properly review a tracker in that time. There are only so many ways to artificially test out how a tracker works, as most cases where you’ll find value in this sort of product can only occur in real life.
So, with that said, let’s focus on the fundamentals.
Google Pixel Tag pairs to your Android phone just like any other Find Hub tracker – though much faster compared to some others I’ve tested – but the differences are obvious towards the end of that process. The final screen shows options for setting ringer volume and an option to set up “Ring this phone.”
Those new features are what make the Pixel Tag so good, and so appealing compared to all of the competition. A quick double-tap on the Tag’s button rings whichever phone you connected it to, assuming it’s in range, and it works pretty reliably. You can also set up “left behind” alerts (now available on other Find Hub trackers too) for when the phone leaves the tracker behind – you can set up exclusion zones such as your home or work address.
One of my favorite examples of the added polish from Google is the ability to adjust the ringer volume on the page where you actually want to ring the tracker. In a crowded but quiet space where you know the tracker is close by, being able to quickly set the volume to low is a great addition. In my book, it’s the reason to buy Pixel Tag over any other Android tracker.
UWB, of course, only makes up-close finding all the better. I found this decently reliable on my Pixel 11 Pro XL, but it is a little bit frustrating that the directional cues vanish within about 10-12 feet. Fine for a backpack or something like that, potentially a problem if your Tag is attached to a set of keys.
On that note, my biggest hardware complaint is that Google took the Apple route of having no built-in mounting mechanism. The super thin and light hardware of Pixel Tag is wonderful, don’t get me wrong, but being forced to buy a separate accessory just to attach it to my bag is frustrating! One of Google’s partners, Bellroy, built one of these accessories and it’s simple enough – a silicone case with a rope. I wish I didn’t need it, but it works, and at least you get two of them in a pack for $25.
The hardware itself is pretty good across the board, really, with the battery door also being slightly easier to open compared to the Moto Tag. Inside is a standard CR2032 battery that Google says will last “over one year.” I’d personally still prefer a rechargeable battery with USB-C or wireless charging, but this is a good enough solution given the amount of time the battery lasts – hopefully Google’s claim lives up.
Rounding out some of the key aspects here, it’s worth saying that the built-in speaker is more than loud enough at its highest setting, but the value for me so far has really come in that the low setting is actually low enough to not be a nuisance. I do find it a little strange that there’s no visual indication of where the Tag’s button is, but the packaging and app both do a good enough job of letting you know.
Overall performance in Find Hub seems fine, but as mentioned at the outset, this is a really hard thing to test artificially, all the more so in the span of just a few days. Google’s Find Hub network has gotten a lot better in the past two years, but it’s still hit or miss in my experience. It’s very clear that Google is making an effort to reverse the privacy-inspired decision to effectively disable the Find Hub network outside of crowded areas, but the damage has been done. I’m not sure the network will ever fully recover from that misstep, regardless of what tracker you’re using it with.
I’m looking forward to seeing how Pixel Tag performs as the travel season spins back up, so stay tuned for a later long-term review of Google’s tracker in the coming months. Initial impressions, though, are solid. Sound off in the comments below if you have any questions around Pixel Tag, I’ll answer everything I can!
If you’re interested in picking up a Pixel Tag, it’ll be available on November 11.

articles.title_orig: Goldman Sachs calls chip stocks 'oversold.' Here are the names it says to buy.
articles.title_zh: Goldman Sachs calls chip stocks 'oversold.' Here are the names it says to buy.
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Goldman Sachs is sifting through the AI stock rubble in search of bargains.
"We believe stocks are now clearly in oversold territory," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider said about semiconductor stocks.
Three of his top names to buy: Nvidia ( NVDA ), Broadcom ( AVGO ), and AMD ( AMD ).
"Even in a 'no growth' scenario for 2028 (which we see as relatively unlikely), NVDA/AVGO are trading 12X/13X this baseline — which we believe valuations are compelling at current levels," Schneider wrote in a note. "We find AMD to be very attractive given the growth we believe it can achieve, albeit at a less compelling valuation."
It has been a brutal run for tech stocks in November.
The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) lost 4.3% of its market value on Nov. 5 as investors assessed what a blue wave on Election Day would mean for the build-out of AI data centers. The move wiped out $3 trillion in value.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) plunged 1,800 points in its worst single-day rout since 2020. The tech-heavy Nasdaq ( ^IXIC ) cratered 5.5%, dragged down by semiconductor and cloud giants such as Micron ( MU ) and Sandisk ( SNDK ).
Stocks have continued to trade with a downward bias, especially semiconductor names.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) is down 21% in the past month, and 6% in November alone.
"We believe the market has been contending with competing tensions relative to semiconductors: (1) How does the funding gap between current capex and free cash flows for hyperscalers and AI model labs levels get closed? (2) Is there sufficient land/power/shell coming on line to match current Street estimates for Semis?" Schneider explained. "Following the US elections on Nov. 3, the second of these tensions came into greater focus with greater uncertainty around the pace of datacenter builds in states such as Texas."
He added, "[Although] we recognize there may be few catalysts for stocks to move higher before year end, we think risk/reward is compelling for select names at current levels."

articles.title_orig: The Culprit Behind Thousands of Ancient Frog Deaths Are Owls
articles.title_zh: The Culprit Behind Thousands of Ancient Frog Deaths Are Owls
articles.content_orig:
The culprits behind a massive frog cemetery that has baffled scientists have turned out to be a group of short-eared owls.
Between 2016 and 2018, 8,000 ancient frog bones were discovered in a single ditch near the site of an Iron Age roundhouse at Bar Hill, near Cambridge.
Scientists at Bournemouth University and Museum of London Archaeology (MOLA) have now identified that birds of prey were behind the 1,700 year-old cold case.
Dr Paul Clarkson, of Bournemouth University, said people "don't often get an owl's eye view of what it was like in the past from archaeological sites".
The researchers compared the damage to the frog bones to previous studies, finding they had most likely been eaten by short-eared owls and hen harriers.
Archaeological evidence also showed the ditch filled within a single year.
The university team used a new method of analysis to discover that most of the frogs died young, having been eaten in the winter of their first year of life.
Radiocarbon dating by the University of Vienna also showed the remains dated back 1,700 years to Roman period.
The fen wetlands were retreating in the valley in the Roman period, creating ideal conditions for the frogs to breed in.
Large areas of woodland were gradually felled over time for grazing livestock, which then left the amphibians with fewer trees to protect them from the grassland hunters.
Clarkson said the solution to the mystery was "a feast of frogs that were eaten and their bones left behind by a group of owls".
"These bones not only tell us about life for people living near the Roman Fens, but they also give insights into the natural world - what wild animals were getting up to in the past, and what life was like for them," he said.
Senior zooarchaeologist Dr Vicki Ewens said she had "so many theories" before the solution was found.
She said the research showed "how even the smallest animal recovered on a site can help us to understand not only past environmental conditions but human activity within a wider landscape".

Death Stranding 2: On the Beach | PS5
Embark on an inspiring mission of human connection beyond the UCA. Join Sam for the next chapter of his journey as he attempts to connect Australia to the Chiral Network. articles.title_orig: Chinese Israel envoy rejects claims Beijing provides military assistance to Iran
articles.title_zh: Chinese Israel envoy rejects claims Beijing provides military assistance to Iran
articles.content_orig:
Shelves were left bare by the cyber-attacks
Iran has described French accusations that it was behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers as "baseless and hostile".
On Monday, the French authorities blamed Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) for the string of hacks, which foreign minister Jean-NoÃ«l Barrot said were "unprecedented" in terms of their scale and "level of aggression".
He added that those responsible would be hit with sanctions.
The French cyber-attacks, which led to the destruction of tons of frozen and chilled food, were followed by a similar hacks against supermarkets across several other European countries. It is not known if the instances are linked.
Barrot said the attack on France's supermarkets "marks the first large-scale cyber-attack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people".
He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act".
France will take "any other necessary and proportionate measures" to respond to the incident and "deter anyone who might seek to repeat it", Barrot added.
The Paris prosecutor, Laure Beccuau, said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with the IRGC as well as his two deputies.
Beccuau named the unit as Shahid Kaveh, which she said had an affiliation with the electronic and cyber centre of the IRGC.
Shahid Kaveh is the name given to a cluster of hackers thought to be directly employed by the Iranian regime.
In recent weeks, a number of commentators and politicians in Iran have argued that the country should extend any retaliation beyond the Middle East if the US and Israel resume the war they started earlier this year.
On Monday, some Iranian media outlets denied the French accusations, but there had been no official comment until Tuesday's statement from Iran's foreign ministry.
On 11 October, hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units used in many of France's supermarkets.
More than 100 of CoopÃ©rative U's supermarkets were hit, as well as 180 stores from IntermarchÃ© and its Netto brand. In some stores, temperatures of the fridges reportedly rose to 50C (120F) overnight.
Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss.
The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely.
Earlier this month a second wave of hacks took place, hitting more than 100 stores across Europe.
Supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in countries including Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland.
Separately in August a small number of US military bases had fridges mysteriously malfunction, spoiling food. This incident is also being investigated as deliberate cyber-attacks, Reuters news agency has reported, citing sources familiar with the matter.
Since the waves of attacks on freezers, experts have been speculating which hacking groups could be responsible, with Iran being on a list of potential suspects.
In spite of a pair of Russian-aligned hacktivist groups claiming they were responsible on Wednesday, few believed them.
The French government has not said how it reached the conclusion that Iran was responsible, and attribution of cyber-attacks is extremely hard as hackers are able to hide their locations.
Additional reporting by Farshad Bayan, BBC Persian.

articles.title_orig: U.S. gas prices fall below $4 for the first time since July
articles.title_zh: U.S. gas prices fall below $4 for the first time since July
articles.content_orig:
Americans may finally find some relief at the pump.
The national average price of regular gasoline fell below $4 a gallon for the first time since July, reaching $3.9788 on Tuesday, according to AAA . Prices are down about 17 cents from a week ago and nearly 39 cents from a month ago.
The decline comes after energy inflation slowed significantly in October. Energy prices increased 0.7% during the month, a far cry from the 5.2% surge seen in September, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics . The BLS' gasoline index increased 1% over the month, after advancing 9.1% in September.
Bespoke Investment Group pointed out that gasoline prices also tend to decline at this time of the year, making part of the recent relief seasonal.
"While lower oil prices have been a tailwind for the relief at the pump, it's also perfectly normal for gas prices to be falling at this time of year, so if they weren't, there would really be something wrong," the firm said.
The drop at the pump followed a sharp retreat in crude oil. International oil benchmark Brent crude on Tuesday briefly fell below $90 a barrel for the first time since August as comments from U.S. President Donald Trump fueled hopes for an end to Washington's nearly nine-month conflict with Iran.
Recovering oil flows from the Persian Gulf have also eased supply concerns. Regional crude exports have returned to an estimated 80% to 85% of prewar levels, including pipeline shipments, according to ING .
"Energy markets remain under pressure as hopes for a de-escalation in the Middle East reduce geopolitical risk premiums. Oil extended its losses as Gulf supply flows continued to recover, while European gas also moved lower," analysts at ING wrote.
However, the Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller warned Tuesday that energy shocks may have more persistent effects on inflation than they did before the pandemic.
"While I am pleased to see energy prices down from their high rates over the past week or so, they are still quite elevated relative to the start of the year, and the ultimate effect on inflation will depend on what levels are sustained," he said.

articles.title_orig: Scion Is Back, and It’s Bringing a Right-Hand Drive 3-Cylinder Kei Truck to the U.S. Market
articles.title_zh: Scion Is Back, and It’s Bringing a Right-Hand Drive 3-Cylinder Kei Truck to the U.S. Market
articles.content_orig:
The kei truck is coming to the US.
Kei vehicles (short for "keijidosha," roughly translated to "light car") are extremely popular and cheap in Japan. The average price for a kei car is typically between $6,000 and $11,000.
On Tuesday, Toyota announced plans to assemble a tiny pickup, the Kei-01, at its Indiana plant in the second half of 2027. It will revive Toyota's low-cost Scion brand, which the automaker discontinued in 2016, and will initially be reserved for commercial fleets.
The Kei-01 is very different from the rest of America's car market. It's nearly 4 feet shorter than a Corolla, gets a motorcycle-sized three-cylinder engine, tops out at 25 mph, and has a steering wheel on the right side.
More importantly, Toyota is joining a fresh set of bets that Americans want cheaper, smaller alternatives to today's big and expensive pickup trucks.
In October, the average transaction price for a new vehicle rose to $51,109, per Kelley Blue Book analysis. That's a record high.
Pickup trucks were the most expensive category, with an average price of $67,912.
America's menu for low-cost car options has been quickly vanishing from car dealership lots. Several sub-$25,000 options — the Mitsubishi Mirage, Nissan Versa, Kia Soul among them — have been discontinued since the end of 2024. Just five new-vehicle models now have an average transaction price below $25,000, according to Cox Automotive.
For years, Americans who wanted a kei truck have largely had to buy old ones. Federal rules allow vehicle imports — even if they don't meet US safety standards — if the car is at least 25 years old. That has created a small but devoted market of car enthusiasts who are looking for their own keis.
Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.
And now, Toyota is the first company to announce plans to build its little truck in the US. The automaker said its truck will have updated safety features, including modern seatbelts, and said it's eligible to drive in all 50 states.
The Kei-01 will be based on the Daihatsu Hijet Jumbo, which sells in Japan for around $9,000. While the company called its US-bound Kei-01 "affordable" in the press release, it hasn't released pricing figures for the American market.
The plan will likely pull on President Donald Trump's heartstrings .
After a 2025 trip to Japan, he has said several times that he wanted companies to start building them in the US.
"I have just approved TINY CARS to be built in America," he wrote on Truth Social in December 2025. "These cars of the very near future are inexpensive, safe, fuel efficient and, quite simply, AMAZING!!! START BUILDING THEM NOW!"
While Toyota is the only car company with concrete US kei truck plans, it's not alone in betting that there is an opening below the increasingly gargantuan full-size pickup. Ford plans to build its sub-$30,000 Fathom EV , while Slate Auto and Telo are developing roughly Mini Cooper-sized electric pickups for the US market.

articles.title_orig: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon with agent ‘swarm’ feature
articles.title_zh: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon with agent ‘swarm’ feature
articles.content_orig:
Developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers can now try our latest frontier model.
SVP, Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect, Google
Your browser does not support the audio element.
Today, we’re making Gemini 4 Carbon available to developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers. Carbon is our strongest model with frontier performance in cybersecurity capabilities and long-horizon agentic workflows across complex knowledge work, software engineering, and scientific reasoning.
Two weeks ago , we released Carbon to a set of cybersecurity defenders via our Fairwind Program . Following our recent launch of Gemini 4 Argon , Carbon pushes the frontier even further. Argon remains the ideal choice for the majority of software engineering and knowledge work, while Carbon is built for tasks that test the limits of a model’s intelligence like complex, multi-step coding and debugging and open-ended scientific research and discovery — using more tokens than Argon to explore thoroughly, reason deeply, and run extended verification loops.
Across independent benchmarks designed to test model performance in real workflows, Carbon pairs frontier accuracy with practical production economics. It ranks #1 on CursorBench 4.0 , Perplexity’s WANDR , and Zapier’s AutomationBench at more than 2X lower cost per task compared to the next best external model.
To put Carbon’s capabilities to work on larger and complex projects, we’re previewing /swarm in Google Antigravity, turning a single prompt into a coordinated team of agents you can track in real time. Developers can assign Carbon to roles that demand the deepest reasoning, like architectural design, coordination, and auditing, while pairing it with faster, lighter models across parallel isolated workspaces and adversarial verifiers that test every change.
Gemini 4 Carbon is available via the API in Google AI Studio and Gemini for business for all paying developers and enterprises, at the same introductory price 1 as Gemini 4 Argon ($2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens). It is also rolling out to all Google AI Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity , the Gemini app , and AI Mode in Search .
Across legal, finance, and enterprise operations, Gemini 4 Carbon combines frontier visual understanding, reasoning, and exhaustive retrieval to synthesize grounded insights across large sets of dense documents and data. It follows strict schemas and formatting to generate polished and precise spreadsheets, presentations, and reports.
Existing benchmarks don’t adequately capture how agents reason natively over dense files with charts, images, blueprints, schematics, and tables, so we partnered with Artificial Analysis to launch the new Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark that tests a model’s multimodal performance in agentic workflows. Carbon ranks #2 while being more than 6X lower in average cost per task compared to the top performing model.
Using Google Antigravity’s new /swarm feature, a team of Gemini 4 Carbon agents turned historical photos and engineering plates into an interactive Three.js 3D exhibition of the Eiffel Tower's 1887–1889 construction from a single prompt.
With seven public City Council planning PDFs (206 extracted engineering drawing views) and a single prompt, a multi-agent Carbon team using Google Antigravity’s /swarm feature built an interactive 906K-triangle Three.js reconstruction of Google’s Platform 37 office across 10 overnight loops.
In Google Antigravity, Gemini 4 Carbon built an interactive multiscale textile visualizer based on an academic paper, modeling a virtual-fiber finite element framework with interactive 3D yarn meshes, 110-fiber polar tracking, and dynamic stress-strain curves with minimal prompting.
In pre-release evaluations, Carbon matched the performance of the best model tested on deep financial research on Hebbia’s E2E Financial Agentic evaluation, and ranked at the top out of 23 frontier model configurations on Balyasny Asset Management’s General Financial Intelligence benchmark, spanning legal expertise, agentic tool use and execution, coding and data engineering, and perception and context understanding.
Carbon performs exceptionally well on engineering tasks that require multi-agent collaboration like multi-package migrations, cross-subsystem root-cause investigations, and complex architectural redesigns. For web app development, it runs build-and-verify loops, recovers from errors, and checks both its code and the rendered UI to produce complete, working applications. Stronger visual design, spatial reasoning, and attention to environmental detail also carry over to 3D game development and creative coding.
Using Google Antigravity’s /swarm feature, Carbon built an open-world 3D game where you explore Google’s Mountain View campus as a pelican riding a GBike — coordinating subagents to model 3D assets in Blender from Omni and Nano Banana references, build the browser game in Three.js with WebGL shaders, and pair procedural Web Audio sound effects with Lyria music. Try the live app .
Paired with improved front end taste and motion design skills in Google Antigravity, Carbon reimagined the Google Merchandise Store in two prompts, proposing five art direction concepts and generating all-new product imagery with Nano Banana 2.1. Try the live app and Gemini front end design skill .
Starting from a video reference generated with Gemini Omni in Google Antigravity, built a cinematic multi-shot underwater Atlantis scene. The pipeline modeled procedural ruins, volumetric caustic lighting, and water simulation in Blender before converting the full environment to Three.js for real-time browser rendering.
Using a multi-agent loop in Google Antigravity, Carbon reconstructed a playable c. 1780 Stein-Schule fortepiano with 61-key escapement physics from CAD drawings and X-ray radiographs and placed it in a 3D model of the Royal Conservatory of Music's Koerner Hall in Toronto with seat-specific spatial acoustics. Try the live app .
Gemini 4 Carbon for cyber delivers our strongest cybersecurity capabilities to date, giving security teams the end-to-end intelligence they need in protecting critical software. When accessed through the Fairwind Program, Carbon leads on key benchmarks across finding (SEC-bench Pro), exploiting (ExploitGym), and patching (CWE-bench v1) vulnerabilities: inspecting software, tracing how flaws can be chained together across systems, and generating verified root-cause patches.
Early testers inside and outside of Google are already seeing strong results with Carbon for cyber in practice.
Gemini 4 Carbon shows strongly improved performance in reasoning across physics, math, and life sciences, synthesizing experimental data, testing hypotheses, and reasoning through multi-step domain problems. For drug toxicity research company Axiom Bio, Carbon is now the leading model in performance for translational science, finding novel mechanisms of toxicity they hadn’t found previously. Axiom is now moving their production scientific analyses and agents to both Carbon and Argon to unlock the creation of safer drugs.
Researchers across Google have been using Carbon in Google Antigravity to accelerate their work:
Four weeks ago, we opened applications to give 10,000 scientists access to Argon in Google Antigravity free of charge for six months to accelerate the pace of their research, and we’ve onboarded thousands of scientists already. Today, we’re expanding access to Carbon for current and future participants, and going forward, the program will continue providing access to our latest frontier models as they become available. Applications remain open and onboarding continues on a weekly rolling basis, subject to eligibility, capacity, and selection.
With each new model release, we continue to strengthen our safety and security mitigations, agentic misuse prevention, model alignment, and harm reduction proportionately with model capability.

articles.title_orig: Board of Peace says Israel's aid response after Gaza floods 'insufficent'
articles.title_zh: Board of Peace says Israel's aid response after Gaza floods 'insufficent'
articles.content_orig:
Winter rain began this weekend in Gaza, where a majority of the population lives in tents and other shelters
US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace has called on Israel to immediately allow all necessary humanitarian supplies into Gaza after rain flooded tens of thousands of tents.
The US-backed body, established to oversee the implementation of Trump's Gaza peace plan, acknowledged the steps now being considered by Israel, but said "the response remains insufficient".
Israel's military agency in charge of co-ordinating aid into Gaza said it had allowed in tens of thousands of tents and trucks with winter supplies, but added reconstruction "can only begin after Hamas fully disarms".
On Sunday, three children and a woman were killed when a sand embankment collapsed onto tents in the central Strip.
Most people in Gaza have been displaced because of Israel's military actions. Around 65% of the population, about 1.4 million people, now live in tents or makeshift shelters, the UN says.
Standing soaked in Gaza City, Mohammed Jneid told the AFP news agency that heavy rains hit from one side and sewage overflowed on them from the other, with the ground and tents no longer able to hold.
"We have nothing left, no bedding, no food, nothing," he said.
Sitting inside her tent, Islam Al Mobayed told AFP there were seven children there, five of them young.
"This is not life," she said. "We are exhausted, we are tired of this entire life."
In rare criticism of Israel, the Board of Peace said it had been urging the Israeli government to authorise the entry of essential goods for temporary shelter and water and sanitation infrastructure.
The Board added that delays in approving the entry of supplies "exacerbated the consequences of a foreseeable humanitarian challenge" and delayed the start of decommissioning weapons and transferring Hamas authority to a transitional government.
It also said Hamas's failure to disarm and transfer power had compounded the difficulties facing Gaza's civilians.
The UN's humanitarian agency OCHA said more than 150,000 tents were outside Gaza ready to go in, but aid efforts were constrained "by Israeli restrictions on the entry of supplies and equipment and funding shortfalls".
UN humanitarian coordinator Ramiz Alakbarov said on Monday that stocks of essential shelter and winter items inside Gaza had been exhausted.
"Israeli authorities must immediately lift all restrictions on entry of the supplies," he said, adding "we have run out of time".
Israel's foreign ministry spokeswoman Michal Maayan on Monday said Israel had in recent months put in place a winter plan in coordination with the Board of Peace and international charities.
That plan has brought in more than 91,000 tents and 8,200-plus trucks with tarpaulins, blankets, winter clothing, and other equipment, according to Cogat, the Israeli military body responsible for aid.
Cogat said it would not allow in equipment that could be used for military purposes.
Maayon accused Hamas of hoarding aid, saying: "Hamas is responsible for the delays in making more progress in the Strip, and winter-related hardships are a consequence of Hamas's action and policy."
In response to the Board of Peace, Hamas said in a statement published on Palestinian media that its comment "presents a distorted account of the causes of the disaster". The group denied it was responsible for ceasefire delays, pointing to a statement in August , external from Egyptian, Qatari and Turkish mediators that accused Israel of violations.
Hamas said Israeli restrictions prevent the entry of materials necessary for shelter and recovery - and added the Board as the ceasefire implementor should look at its own "serious shortcoming".
Under the deal to end the two-year-long war in October 2025, Hamas agreed to give up governance and its weapons in exchange for a phased Israeli troop withdrawal from the 60% of Gaza it still occupied. Israel, however, has insisted Hamas must fully disarm before withdrawal.
The dispute has left the next stages of the peace plan stalled, with both sides blaming each other.
The war in Gaza began after the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 when around 1,200 people were killed and 251 others taken hostage.
The Israeli military campaign in response has killed 74,645 people, according to the Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures the UN considers reliable. More than 1,600 people have been killed since the ceasefire in October last year.
Israel says six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza since then.

articles.title_orig: Galaxy S27 redesign leak shows off Pro vs Ultra size difference, with just a bit of controversy
articles.title_zh: Galaxy S27 redesign leak shows off Pro vs Ultra size difference, with just a bit of controversy
articles.content_orig:
Samsung is working on a long overdue redesign for its Galaxy S27 series and, this week, we’re getting a fresh look.
We’ve already seen it in renders, but leaker Sonny Dickson took to Twitter/X today to present an image of Galaxy S27 Pro, Ultra, and S27+ dummy units, and it tells us a few things.
First, we get to see the redesign again, this time in “real life.” That’s, of course, with the caveat that these aren’t real devices, and probably aren’t reflective of the final design either. The Pro and Ultra both have a full-width camera island akin to Apple’s latest iPhone design language, and a big departure from the vertical camera array that Samsung insisted was its “core identity” mere months ago.
Importantly, we can also see the size difference between Galaxy S27 Ultra and S27 Pro, with the Pro being noticeably smaller compared to both the Ultra and the S27+. For small(er) phone fans, it’s looking great .
All of that said, adding a bit of controversy to this image is leaker Ice Universe, who says “this picture is wrong.”
Ice points out that the Galaxy S27 Ultra and Pro both do not have a fourth camera lens, which is correct based on recent leaks . That said, it’s not much of a leap to assume these dummy units are based on an older design, or are confusing a sensor. After all, these are mainly used to test accessories and, this early on, there’s plenty of room for inaccuracy.
What do you think of this image? Do you think it’ll look like the final product? Do you like the size difference on the Galaxy S27 Pro?

articles.title_orig: CoreWeave earnings put debt-fueled AI build-out under scrutiny
articles.title_zh: CoreWeave earnings put debt-fueled AI build-out under scrutiny
articles.content_orig:
CoreWeave faces a pivotal test when it reports its third-quarter financial results after the bell on Tuesday.
The market will be closely watching what the neocloud company says about artificial intelligence spending — and how it plans to finance its infrastructure buildout. The outcome could either calm concerns over its debt or stoke more fear.
"Investors need neoclouds to quantify how much financing they expect to raise to execute on existing backlog," Wolfe Research said in a note Monday. "We think outlooks that communicate when and which avenues of funding will be tapped will increase investor confidence."
CoreWeave stock and bonds have come under pressure as fears deepened about the enormous amount of debt it has taken out to build its data centers.
Its stock is down roughly 40% over the past month. Meanwhile, the yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 15.5% on Tuesday, after jumping to 16.7% on Thursday as investors digested the election results and possible roadblocks to data center construction. Bond yields move inversely to prices.
The spread on its five-year credit default swaps — which is insurance against default and considered a barometer of perceived credit risk — is also at levels that are considered distressed. On Tuesday, its CDS spread stood around 1,152 basis points, after rising above its October peak to close at 1,278 basis points on Thursday. Rising CDS spreads mean investors view the debt as riskier.
In addition, the New Jersey-based company's leverage is high. CoreWeave has a debt-to-equity ratio of 702%, up from almost 291% a year ago.
CEO Michael Intrator has sought to quell investor fear, posting on LinkedIn after the election last week that the company doesn't anticipate "any impact to CoreWeave's existing customer commitments or associated backlog as a result of shifts in the political landscape."
The company reported a revenue backlog of $104.2 billion in the second quarter . It has about $35 billion in debt, as of June 30.
CoreWeave has already given a picture of what it expects for the third quarter.
It guided for quarterly revenue of $3.4 billion to $3.6 billion when it reported second-quarter results in August. It anticipated capital expenditures between $11.5 billion and $13.5 billion for the quarter and $35 billion to $39 billion for the full year. The company also expects 1.85 gigawatts in active power by year-end.
Wells Fargo expects the company's capex needs for the rest of the year to be largely covered by its remaining undrawn debt, debt issuances in August/September and the $12 billion it is holding for project costs, which will flow into capex, analyst Michael Turrin said in a note Sunday.
However, its 2027 capex could reach $66 billion, based on an expected capacity addition of 1.5 gigawatts, Turrin said. That will require at least $25 billion more in debt, he noted. It can be largely funded through delayed draw term loans, which allows CoreWeave to draw down funds over time, and the rest can come through bonds and convertibles, he said.
Turrin has an overweight rating and $115 price target on the stock, implying 135% upside from Monday's close.
"While neoclouds sit in the eye of the AI storm, we remain confident that CRWV is the highest quality co in the space," Turrin wrote. "Beyond the noise, we see capacity/revs coming in better than expected (1.95GW this yr vs guide 1.85GW) as margins start to inflect."
However, investors likely won't get all the answers they're seeking during CoreWeave's third-quarter results, said CreditSights analyst Jordan Chalfin.
"One of the major issues for CoreWeave is whether or not they can obtain all the financing they need," he said. "They may try and calm the markets, but I'm not sure how much color they can and will provide."
Investors will be looking for 2027 guidance on capex and free cash flow, though that may not come until Coreweave releases fourth quarter results, Chalfin notes.
CoreWeave could ease investor concerns by showing it has plans and approvals in place to scale capacity through 2027, he said. The company can also demonstrate remaining performance obligation (RPO) growth, which shows the total value of its contracted future revenue, and highlight new customer wins.
In addition, pricing has been really strong on recent deals, Chalfin pointed out. "That could show up in an operating margin beat for Q3 and expectations for Q4."
While CoreWeave faces finances challenges, the company has many ways to access capital, Chalfin said. That includes chip-backed deals, which allow Corewave to borrow money using GPUs as collateral, and original equipment manufacturer financing. For instance, CoreWeave could turn to Dell , which is a big supplier with a strong balance sheet, Chalfin noted.
"Despite all the market sentiment, fundamentals are actually quite strong and pricing is strong," he said. "The trends over the next few quarters, I think, should be supportive." Risks could arise after that, but it is "too early to call."
Some analysts remain skeptical that Coreweave will be able to calm credit fears.
Bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, points out that the company is facing a huge bill in just over two years. CoreWeave owes roughly $15 billion in principal payments through 2028, according to its second-quarter earnings statement .
"They don't have enough cash to service all that debt," he said. "Unless some big orders come in, unless some big money flows come in for them in the next 17, 18 months, I think this is going to be the start of the end for CoreWeave, unless somebody comes in and wants to buy them. But who wants to buy all that debt?"
However, there could be a "small" window for the company to push out its debt for another three to five years, but it will depend on how strong their cash flow is when they report on Tuesday, Lang said.
Plus, issuing equity to help fund infrastructure projects, like Meta and Oracle did recently , isn't an option for CoreWeave, he noted.
"They're going to dilute the stock so much that it's going to continue to go down," he said. "They missed that window when the stock was in the hundreds."
CoreWeave topped $183 in June 2025. It has since declined more than 73%, recently trading around $47.
Despite the fall, analysts remain bullish on the stock with an average overweight rating and $126 target, based on 39 estimates complied by FactSet.
—CNBC's Jordan Novet contributed reporting.

articles.title_orig: Samsung Gallery officially adds Google Photos backup, but not for all Galaxy users
articles.title_zh: Samsung Gallery officially adds Google Photos backup, but not for all Galaxy users
articles.content_orig:
Samsung has officially launched Google Photos integration in its Gallery app with backup services, and it’s also now widely rolled out for Galaxy devices.
Samsung Gallery started rolling out support for Google Photos backup in September, but it wasn’t widely available at the time. As of this week, though, Samsung is officially announcing the feature as it is now available broadly to Galaxy users.
“Gallery Sync” in the Samsung Gallery app replaces the previous Microsoft OneDrive integration with Google Photos, letting users sign in with their Google account of choice and use the free 15GB or paid Google One storage to back up photos and videos. This allows the Samsung Gallery app to show media backed up from another Galaxy device, but it doesn’t integrate your full Google Photos library.
At this point, Google Photos backup via Samsung Gallery should be broadly available to Galaxy owners. We’re seeing Samsung’s pop-up (pictured above) about the feature on our Galaxy Z Fold 8, with the feature fully functional beyond that.
You can also access setup via Menu > Settings > “Sync photos and videos” in the Samsung Gallery app.
Samsung requires your device to be running One UI 9 (Android 17) to access this feature, though it says that support will be “expanding to additional Galaxy devices in phases.” For the time being, though, that means the feature is a bit limited for users, as the One UI 9 rollout is still in progress.
Once media has been backed up to Google Photos, Samsung Gallery also now has a “free up space” button that can delete the local copies of your photos and videos to open up storage on your phone.

articles.title_zh: Holy Crap: The Ford Mustang Cobra Is Coming Back
articles.content_orig:
Fresh details about the Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 successor suggest that the upcoming model will be offered exclusively as a coupe.
Unlike the more powerful Dark Horse SC, which is available with both a fixed roof and a soft-top convertible, the new variant will not get an open-top version. This also follows the approach taken with the previous S550-generation Shelby GT350, which was sold only as a coupe.
Pricing is expected to position the car between the standard Dark Horse and the Dark Horse SC. The 2026 Dark Horse starts at around $65,000, while the SC carries a much higher starting price of approx $106,000. A price in the $80,000 range could make sense for the new model, although Ford has yet to confirm anything.
Its official name remains under wraps, but the Dark Horse badge is expected to feature somewhere in it. The new Mustang is reportedly scheduled to reach dealerships in 2027 as a 2027 model-year offering.

articles.title_orig: Number of arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
articles.title_zh: Number of arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
articles.content_orig:
French police have made arrests after three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, were searched in relation to an investigation into Mohamed Al Fayed's abuse.
The Paris prosecutor's office told the BBC that several individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and later released.
In a confidential letter sent to survivors, the Metropolitan Police said its officers were present during the searches on 13 and 14 October, in what is understood to be a joint operation between British and French authorities.
It is the first time any arrests have been made in relation to alleged abuse and trafficking by the former Harrods and Ritz owner.
Several victims of Al Fayed were also interviewed by French investigators, the prosecutor's office said.
It added that the searches were part of a preliminary investigation into "allegations of human trafficking committed by an organized group, aggravated pimping committed by an organized group, and rape".
The investigation is ongoing and digital material seized during the searches is being analysed.
The late Egyptian billionaire bought the Ritz Paris hotel in 1979, and it is still owned by the Al Fayed family.
The Villa Windsor in western Paris, another property involved in the search, was a holiday home for the Al Fayed family. It was previously the home of King Edward VIII, following his abdication, and his wife Wallis Simpson.
The Met shared this statement from French authorities with victims:
"At this stage of the proceedings, several victims have been interviewed by French investigators, and the investigations are being conducted in liaison with the British authorities.
"In this context, searches and evidence-gathering operations were carried out in mid-October 2026, notably within the Hotel Ritz in the 1st arrondissement of Paris, as well as at the Villa Sainte-Thérèse in Saint-Tropez, a former property of Mohamed Al Fayed, and at the Villa Windsor in the 16th arrondissement of Paris, in the presence of British investigators.
"Several suspects were taken into police custody, measures which were lifted following their interviews, specifically for the purpose of analyzing digital material seized during the search operations.
"The investigations are continuing under the direction of the Paris Public Prosecutor's Office."
A Met Police spokesperson confirmed its officers travelled to France in October and were present during the operation.
Al Fayed, who died in 2023 aged 94, was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC documentary and podcast in September 2024.
One of the women featured in the documentary said she was sexually assaulted by Al Fayed at the Ritz hotel in Paris, while another woman said she had been raped by him at the Villa Windsor residence.
Since those allegations, more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers.
A woman has also told BBC Scotland she was trafficked, drugged, sexually assaulted and held prisoner on the Balnagown Estate by Al Fayed's brother , Salah Fayed, who died in 2010.
Both brothers died without facing legal charges in relation to these allegations.
Earlier this year, Police Scotland said it was carrying out further investigations into allegations connected to Balnagown Estate.
In a statement, a force spokesperson said: "Three people have been identified in connection with offending against a number of victims.
"Our inquiries are ongoing and it would be inappropriate to comment further."
The Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors group said it welcomed the "significant developments" and cooperation between the Met and French authorities.
"We believe that all properties owned by Fayed should be investigated with the same thoroughness as those already searched, wherever they are located, to ensure that no potentially relevant evidence is overlooked," the group said.
"We hope these developments represent meaningful progress towards identifying and holding to account all those who facilitated, concealed or assisted his offending, wherever they operated."
The survivor advocacy group No One Above said: "France is treating this as organised human trafficking, led by specialists, with properties searched and evidence seized. That is what a serious investigation into a network looks like.
"Two years on, survivors are still waiting for the same from the Met. It is time the National Crime Agency took this investigation over."
The management of the Ritz Paris told AFP news agency that it "does not tolerate any form of harassment, abuse or inappropriate behaviour" and that it was ready "to cooperate fully with the competent judicial authorities".
